subject.title: fix(android): stop push-to-talk from dropping speech after mid-hold pauses

question: Should this Android lifecycle change proceed after real-device proof covers the raw-audio, silence-segmented, and restart fallback rungs?
rationale: Automated tests cover the intended callback ordering, but Android documents the relevant recognizer extras as implementation-dependent; only an owner can accept device/service coverage sufficient for this microphone-capture change.

options.title: Require device proof before merge
options.body: Capture redacted after-fix evidence for a paused multi-sentence hold, release timing, and a fallback-capable recognizer before approving the current implementation.

options.title: Accept limited-service risk
options.body: Merge with the supplied Robolectric coverage while accepting that recognizer-specific raw and segmented behavior remains unverified on hardware.

recommendation.title: Require device proof before merge
recommendation.body: Capture redacted after-fix evidence for a paused multi-sentence hold, release timing, and a fallback-capable recognizer before approving the current implementation.
